item.description: Quelque 161.000 foyers étaient privés d'électricité vendredi matin dans l'ouest de la France balayé par la tempête Austen, la première de l'automne, qui s'accompagne de vents violents, rapporte Enedis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Quelque 161.000 foyers étaient privés d'électricité vendredi matin dans l'ouest de la France balayé par la tempête Austen, la première de l'automne, qui s'accompagne de vents violents, rapporte Enedis. "Dans une situation encore très évolutive, car la tempête est toujours en cours, les régions les plus touchées sont la Bretagne (128 000 clients), les Pays de la Loire (19 000 clients) et la Normandie (14 000 clients)", a précisé dans un communiqué la filiale d'EDF chargée de la gestion du réseau public de distribution d'électricité. Météo France a placé en vigilance orange pour vents violents 23 départements de la façade nord-ouest, de la Bretagne aux Hauts-de-France et jusqu'à Paris et l'Ile-de-France. "Au sud de la dépression, un épisode de vent fort et tempétueux s'est mis en place en cours de nuit de jeudi à vendredi; il va se décaler vers l'est en journée de vendredi", a expliqué l'agence. Des rafales de 120 à 140 km/h ont été observées la nuit dernière sur le littoral breton et le littoral ouest du département de la Manche, a-t-elle précisé.

item.title: Heineken document reveals worries over weight-loss drugs and beer sales
item.description: Heineken has urged British pubs and bars to adapt to the booming use of weight-loss drugs or risk losing customers and revenue, according to a company presentation seen by Reuters, in a rare acknowledgement from a major alcohol maker that the medicines pose a threat to beer sales.
item.dc:creator: Emma Rumney
item.content:encoded: Heineken (HEIN.AS) has urged British pubs and bars to adapt to the booming use of weight-loss drugs or risk losing customers and revenue, according to a company presentation seen by Reuters, in a rare acknowledgement from a major alcohol maker that the medicines pose a threat to beer sales. The warning comes as GLP-1 use has surged, with some 10 million people taking medications like Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) Ozempic and Wegovy in the US last year, according to JPMorgan research. Their growth is having ramifications across the consumer goods industry, hitting [USN:L6N44E0VN TEXT:"cravings for sweets and snacks"], driving up [USN:L6N45R11L TEXT:"demand for clothing alterations"] and prompting a scramble to sell products that [USN:L6N4500ZA TEXT:"counter side-effects"]. Heineken, the world's second-largest brewer after AB InBev told hospitality customers that GLP-1 drugs can reduce the desire to drink and put pressure on beer and cider sales from "fullness and fewer serves", while warning that traditional multi-pint drinking occasions could become harder to sustain. The previously unreported presentation, sent to hospitality customers this month, advised venues to promote half-pints, low- and no-alcohol drinks and pair drinks with small plates, or risk declines in customer visits and spending as use of the medicines becomes increasingly mainstream in Britain. The alcohol industry is already grappling with years of falling sales in some major markets as consumers cut back on drinking for health and economic reasons. Heineken told Reuters the presentation was shared as part of its regular engagement with UK hospitality businesses to help them understand how the market is evolving. "We see some changes in consumption behaviour among (GLP-1) users and will continue to monitor how these behaviours evolve in 2027," Heineken said. GLP-1 users were not abandoning alcohol altogether but were increasingly opting for smaller serves, lower-alcohol drinks and more premium products, aligning with broader ongoing trends, it continued, adding its portfolio is well positioned to meet these demands. EVIDENCE OF REDUCED CONSUMPTION GROWS Europe is the Dutch brewer's largest market by revenue, but growth has been sluggish. Heineken has singled out Britain, where it owns more than 2,000 pubs, as a relative bright spot. Beer generated nearly £14 billion of sales in British pubs, bars and restaurants in the year to February 2026, with less than £300 million of that from no- and low-alcohol beers, according to a Heineken UK report. Although drinks companies have largely played down the threat from GLP-1 medicines, emerging spending data points to an impact on purchases. A group of US households with a GLP-1 user tracked by market research firm Circana between 2024 and 2026 reduced spending on alcohol for both at-home and out-of-home consumption compared with households without a user. After two years on the drugs, they spent about 7% less per month on alcohol versus non-using households, including around 13.5% less on beer. Top spirits maker Diageo (DGE.L) has told investors any impact from GLP-1 drugs should be manageable even if use becomes more widespread. Carlsberg (CARLb.CO) told Reuters existing data did not yet support the view that the drugs were a clear driver of beer consumption trends. Anheuser-Busch InBev (ABI.BR) declined to comment. Surveys in Europe and the UK by Circana, market researcher NIQ and specialist UK-based hospitality researcher KAM have also pointed to reduced drinking by GLP-1 users. Ten of 11 GLP-1 users Reuters interviewed said they had reduced their drinking, sometimes significantly, saying it left them feeling uncomfortable or unwell, or they simply no longer had any desire to drink. UK-based Daniel Cornell, founder of hospitality executive recruitment business SPE Resourcing, said he used to drink regularly at work events and on weekends but now finds alcohol causes him discomfort and results in a multi-day hangover. GLP-1's effects on the brain may also affect users' motivation to drink, said Joseph Schacht, a professor at the University of Colorado Anschutz, who led a randomised controlled trial on the impact of GLP-1s on people with alcohol use disorder. He said trials have consistently shown a reduction in cravings and consumption for people with AUD. Schacht said the medicines could create a potential "Prozac moment" for AUD treatment, while also posing a challenge for alcohol producers if broader groups of drinkers cut back too.

item.title: Signify beats profit expectations helped by US tariff refund
item.description: The world's largest lighting maker Signify beat third-quarter core profits expectations on Friday, helped by an extraordinary US tariff refund and reduced costs of sales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The world's largest lighting maker Signify (LIGHT.AS) beat third-quarter core profits expectations on Friday, helped by an extraordinary US tariff refund and reduced costs of sales. Following the tariff refund, the company now expects to reach the top end of its annual guidance for adjusted EBITA margin range of 7.5% to 8.5%. Signify posted quarterly adjusted earnings before interest, taxes and amortisation (EBITA) of €145 million ($163 million), above the €113 million average analysts' forecast seen in a company-compiled poll. The US tariff refund resulted in a benefit of €28 million. The group reported quarterly sales falling to €1.37 billion, in line with expectations, and said it still expects persistent challenging market conditions in its European and US businesses. Signify, which spun off from Philips (PHG.AS) in 2016, had earlier in the year [USN:L6N42V0AR TEXT:"announced"] a new dividend policy and medium-term targets, which failed to convince investors of an imminent turnaround. The turnaround story included a portfolio review, which would reduce Signify's in-house manufacturing of standard lighting products as it struggled with Chinese overcapacity. ($1 = 0.8921 euros)

item.title: South Korea proposes talks with North Korea on land border again
item.description: South Korea's defence ministry again proposed on Friday military talks with North Korea in order to agree on the exact location of the land border between the two Koreas and to reduce the risk of accidental clashes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's defence ministry again proposed on Friday military talks with North Korea in order to agree on the exact location of the land border between the two Koreas and to reduce the risk of accidental clashes. The proposal, announced by Deputy Minister for National Defense Policy Kim Hong-cheol, follows a landmine explosion in the demilitarised zone (DMZ) last month that injured South Korean soldiers. North Korean troops have been building tactical roads and fences and laying mines near the Military Demarcation Line (MDL) in the DMZ separating the two Koreas in recent years. Kim said the North's troops had crossed the line in the process. The ministry proposed talks last November to resolve differences over where the line lies, but Pyongyang has not responded. South Korean military had concluded that North Korea had buried the mines south of the MDL that caused the blast that seriously injured two South Korean soldiers in September. Pyongyang has rejected those findings.

item.title: Eni to pay special dividend, lift buyback after strong third-quarter results
item.description: Italy's Eni will pay a €1.3 billion special dividend and slightly increase its share buyback programme after posting a third-quarter net profit that more than doubled from a year earlier, the energy group said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's Eni (ENI.MI) will pay a €1.3 billion special dividend and slightly increase its share buyback programme after posting a third-quarter net profit that more than doubled from a year earlier, the energy group said on Friday. The state-controlled company said its adjusted net profit in the July-September period was €2.8 billion, above a company-compiled analyst consensus of €2.48 billion and up from €1.25 billion a year earlier. Eni also raised its guidance for underlying cash flow from operations (CFFO) to €16.5 billion from a previous €15 billion. "We are further raising the distribution by an extraordinary dividend of €0.46 per share to be paid in the fourth-quarter and increasing again the buyback to €3.8 bln, underscoring our continued commitment to sharing upside with shareholders," CEO Claudio Descalzi said in a statement.

item.title: South Korean economy's growth likely picked up in Q3 on chip exports: Reuters poll
item.description: South Korea's economy grew slightly faster in the third quarter than in April to June, as booming semiconductor exports and AI-related investment helped offset still-uneven domestic demand, a Reuters poll of economists showed.
item.dc:creator: Renusri K
item.content:encoded: South Korea's economy grew slightly faster in the third quarter than in April to June, as booming semiconductor exports and AI-related investment helped offset still-uneven domestic demand, a Reuters poll of economists showed. An AI-fuelled chip boom has supported South Korea's economy for years, but has also made it increasingly reliant on chip exports, with the gains yet to spread widely through the domestic economy. Meanwhile, high borrowing costs and elevated household debt have weighed on household consumption. Exports rose 84% from a year earlier to a record $120.9 billion in [USN:L1N45N002 TEXT:"September"], led by a 262.8% surge in chip exports to $60.3 billion. Semiconductors accounted for nearly half of total shipments, underlining the industry's outsized role in driving gross domestic product growth. The economy grew a seasonally adjusted 0.7% in the July-September quarter, according to the median forecast of 16 economists polled from October 14-23, a slight pickup from 0.6% growth in the April-June quarter. Forecasts ranged from 0.5% to 1.6%. "The question is whether we will see benefits from the export sector. It is important to see the transmission to the domestic economy, and one of the key channels is fiscal policy to ease the pressures," said Jeong Woo Park, Asia economist at Nomura. "Financial conditions are becoming less accommodative and the labour market is structurally in downturn. With companies adopting AI more rapidly, for the younger generation it is very hard to find jobs," Park said. The contrast between the fast-growing chip sector and softer demand elsewhere in the economy has raised concerns among some economists that the recovery, which began in the first quarter, is becoming increasingly uneven. On a year-on-year basis, GDP was forecast to grow 3.0%, slowing from 3.7% in the previous quarter, based on the median estimate from 16 economists. "The concentration risk of growth being driven by AI should worry the BOK to some extent, but I don't think they are showing it too much," said Kelvin Lam, senior economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics. "The Korean economy is very vulnerable to this as everything now is driven mainly by the semiconductor industry." The [USN:L4N467041 TEXT:"Bank of Korea held"] its benchmark interest rate at 3.00% on Thursday, in line with consensus expectations, and raised its growth forecast to 3.3% for this year and 2.9% for next year. A separate [USN:L6N46505J TEXT:"Reuters poll"] forecast growth of 3.5% in 2026.

item.title: India's Kishan ruled out of second New Zealand T20 with adductor strain

item.title: Swedish defence group Saab's profit beats forecast as sales soar
item.description: Swedish defence and aerospace group Saab reported on Friday a bigger-than-expected rise in third-quarter profit on the back of soaring sales as it continued to ride a wave of global rearmament.
item.dc:creator: Johan Ahlander
item.content:encoded: Swedish defence and aerospace group Saab (SAABb.ST) reported on Friday a bigger-than-expected rise in third-quarter profit on the back of soaring sales as it continued to ride a wave of global rearmament. Operating profit at the maker of the Gripen fighter jet rose to 1.95 billion crowns ($197 million) from 1.37 billion a year earlier, against a 1.91 billion mean forecast in an LSEG poll of analysts. "The long-term market outlook remains favourable," CEO Micael Johansson said in a statement. "With a strong portfolio, a record high order backlog, expanding production capacity and continued investment in future capabilities, we are well positioned to achieve our financial targets," he said. Saab, which also makes military equipment ranging from missiles and advanced electronics to submarines, said in a statement that like-for-like sales rose 30.6% year-on-year. Already riding consecutive years of surging demand driven by rapid rearmament across much of Europe due to Russia's war in Ukraine, the pace has picked up further for Saab this year with a string of huge orders. Saab, which competes with giants such as US-based Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) , France's Dassault Aviation (AM.PA) and Britain's BAE Systems (BAES.L) , said order bookings soared 216% year-on-year in the quarter, including a 24.6 billion crown Gripen order from [USN:L1N4320W8 TEXT:"Ukraine"].

item.title: Le séisme au Tibet a fait 16 morts et 65 blessés
item.description: Le séisme de magnitude 7 survenu au Tibet a fait 16 morts et 65 blessés, a annoncé vendredi le gouvernement local sur les réseaux sociaux.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le séisme de magnitude 7 survenu au Tibet a fait 16 morts et 65 blessés, a annoncé vendredi le gouvernement local sur les réseaux sociaux. L'épicentre du séisme a touché la petite ville de Nagqu, dans le nord du Tibet. Plus de 300 policiers ont été déployés sur place afin de mener les opérations de secours et d'urgence, a dit la police de Nagqu. Plus de 12.000 personnes ont été évacuées, a indiqué l'agence de presse officielle chinoise Xinhua. Le Centre chinois des réseaux sismiques (CENC) a déclaré que 413 répliques avaient été enregistrées. En 2010, un tremblement de terre de magnitude 7,1 a touché Yushu, préfecture autonome tibétaine située dans la province du Qinghai, tuant au moins 2.698 personnes et faisant près de 300 disparus.

item.title: Testing firm SGS posts higher Q3 sales, confirms outlook
item.description: Swiss testing and inspection group SGS reported a 14.6% jump in its third-quarter sales to 1.98 billion Swiss francs ($2.41 billion) on Friday, helped by acquisitions and growth in cybersecurity and sustainability-related services.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swiss testing and inspection group SGS (SGSN.S) reported a 14.6% jump in its third-quarter sales to 1.98 billion Swiss francs ($2.41 billion) on Friday, helped by acquisitions and growth in cybersecurity and sustainability-related services. The company, which has completed 18 acquisitions so far this year, confirmed its financial targets for 2026, including 5% to 7% organic sales growth and an adjusted operating margin of at least 16%. This year's acquisitions are now expected to contribute around 7% to SGS's annual growth, at the top end of its previous 5-7% range, CEO Geraldine Picaud told journalists Acquisitions announced in 2026 represent total annual sales of more than 150 million francs Revenue in Digital Trust, SGS's cybersecurity and digital assurance business, rose 37% in the third quarter Picaud said Digital Trust was approaching 300 million francs in annual revenue She also said SGS would unveil a "very ambitious objective for the years to come" at its November capital markets day ($1 = 0.8215 Swiss francs)

item.title: Volvo Cars affiche une perte au T3, prévoit la suppression de 2.500 emplois
item.description: Volvo Cars a affiché vendredi une perte d'exploitation au troisième trimestre, impacté par la lente montée en puissance de la production de son nouveau SUV électrique EX60 et la faiblesse de la demande en Chine et aux États-Unis, et a annoncé la suppression de 2.500 emplois pour réduire ses coûts face à la concurrence chinoise.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volvo Cars (VOLCARb.ST) a affiché vendredi une perte d'exploitation au troisième trimestre, impacté par la lente montée en puissance de la production de son nouveau SUV électrique EX60 et la faiblesse de la demande en Chine et aux États-Unis, et a annoncé la suppression de 2.500 emplois pour réduire ses coûts face à la concurrence chinoise. La société, détenue majoritairement par le groupe chinois Geely Holding [RIC:RIC:GEELY.UL], a enregistré une perte d'exploitation ajustée de 3,7 milliards de couronnes suédoises (332,78 millions d'euros) au troisième trimestre, contre un bénéfice de 5,8 milliards de couronnes un an plus tôt. “Le troisième trimestre 2026 a été très décevant et reflète une année qui s’est avérée bien plus difficile que prévu initialement. Notre plan de redressement en cours doit donc être renforcé de manière décisive”, a déclaré le directeur général Hakan Samuelsson dans un communiqué. Volvo Cars a déclaré qu'en plus des réductions de coûts déjà mises en œuvre, le groupe allait réduire de 5 milliards de couronnes supplémentaires ses dépenses indirectes et ses coûts variables, une mesure qui devrait être effective d'ici la fin de l'année prochaine. Quelque 2.500 emplois seront supprimés à l'échelle mondiale, dont 2.000 en Suède, le groupe mettant fin aux contrats des consultants, recourant aux départs naturels et proposant des "plans de départ ciblés" à ses salariés, a indiqué Volvo Cars dans un communiqué. Ces nouveaux licenciements s'ajoutent aux 3.000 suppressions d'emplois annoncées peu après le retour de Hakan Samuelsson à son poste, lorsque Volvo Cars a mis en place un plan de réduction des coûts de 18 milliards de couronnes à l'échelle de l'entreprise et renforcé sa coopération avec les marques du groupe Geely. [USN:L8N45O0DO TEXT:"Au début du mois"], le groupe a annoncé qu'il ne serait pas en mesure d'atteindre ses prévisions de volumes et de flux de trésorerie pour 2026, invoquant une situation de marché difficile et une détérioration des perspectives à court terme. Le cours de l'action a atteint un plus bas historique cette semaine et a baissé de 54% depuis le début de l'année, plombé par les droits de douane, la faiblesse de la demande en véhicules électriques et des coûts de développement élevés.

item.title: Les USA se félicitent des progrès réalisés dans les négociations de réconciliation politique au Venezuela
item.description: Le département d'Etat américain s'est félicité jeudi de la conclusion d'un troisième cycle de négociations dans le cadre de la réconciliation politique au Venezuela.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le département d'Etat américain s'est félicité jeudi de la conclusion d'un troisième cycle de négociations dans le cadre de la réconciliation politique au Venezuela. Le processus "continue de renforcer les institutions démocratiques" et de "jeter les bases d'élections libres, équitables et crédibles" dans le pays, a estimé le département d'Etat. Les Etats-Unis continuent d'appeler à la libération immédiate de tous les prisonniers politiques au Venezuela, a dit le porte-parole du département, Tommy Pigott, dans un communiqué. Des milliers de Vénézuéliens sont descendus dans la rue jeudi pour [USN:L6N4681G2 TEXT:"réclamer"] la tenue d'élections libres et d'autres changements politiques.

item.title: Manifestations au Venezuela, les premières en deux ans, pour réclamer des élections libres
item.description: Des milliers de Vénézuéliens sont descendus jeudi dans la rue pour réclamer la tenue d'élections libres et d'autres changements politiques, dans ce qui constitue les premières manifestations à travers le pays d'Amérique latine en près de deux ans, quelques mois après la chute de Nicolas Maduro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des milliers de Vénézuéliens sont descendus jeudi dans la rue pour réclamer la tenue d'élections libres et d'autres changements politiques, dans ce qui constitue les premières manifestations à travers le pays d'Amérique latine en près de deux ans, quelques mois après la chute de Nicolas Maduro. Un gouvernement intérimaire, dirigé par la présidente par intérim Delcy Rodriguez, est en place depuis que les Etats-Unis ont effectué en janvier dernier une opération militaire pour capturer le président Nicolas Maduro. Le président américain Donald Trump, dont l'administration travaille désormais étroitement avec Caracas, scellant notamment des accords pétroliers, a déclaré par le passé que les conditions n'étaient pas réunies dans l'immédiat pour organiser des élections au Venezuela. Delcy Rodriguez, qui était la vice-présidente de Nicolas Maduro, a promis la tenue d'élections, sans toutefois fixer de calendrier, que ce soit pour des législatives ou une présidentielle. La cheffe de file de l'opposition Maria Corina Machado, récompensée l'an dernier du prix Nobel de la paix et qui vit en exil, appelle à des élections d'ici à juillet 2027. Son mouvement, Vente Venezuela, a organisé le rassemblement de jeudi, qui s'est tenu dans la capitale Caracas ainsi que dans d'autres villes dont Valence, Maracay, San Cristóbal et Maracaibo. Le Parti socialiste au pouvoir a appelé ses partisans à défiler depuis la Plaza Venezuela de Caracas – là où l'opposition prévoyait de se rassembler deux heures plus tard – jusqu’à un lieu situé près du palais présidentiel, afin de commémorer le mois de sensibilisation au cancer du sein. Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Diosdado Cabello, connu pour ses liens étroits avec les services de sécurité, a été filmé par la télévision publique alors qu’il assistait au défilé, tandis que les partisans de l’opposition déplaçaient leur manifestation vers un lieu voisin.

item.title: A Ukrainian soldier severed his own foot to survive. Then came a dramatic rescue.
item.description: Kostiantyn Vlasenko was huddled in a hole under the boiler of a bombed-out school when he came to a terrifying conclusion: To survive, he needed to amputate his only remaining foot.
item.dc:creator: Mariano Zafra, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Kostiantyn Vlasenko was huddled in a hole under the boiler of a bombed-out school when he came to a terrifying conclusion: To survive, he needed to amputate his only remaining foot. The Ukrainian infantryman had already lost his left foot in a Russian drone strike in February. His right leg was broken and bent in the same attack, hindering his ability even to crawl. About three months later, after working up the courage, he grabbed his knife, sliced off his foot and applied a tourniquet to staunch the bleeding. He survived. Click here to read more.

item.title: Rexel relève à nouveau ses objectifs avec les USA et l'électrification en Europe
item.description: Rexel a relevé jeudi ses objectifs annuels pour la deuxième fois cette année, la forte demande des centres de données aux États-Unis et l'essor de l'électrification en Europe ayant porté les ventes trimestrielles du distributeur français de matériel électrique de 11,4% sur un an.
item.dc:creator: Leo Marchandon, Matthieu Huchet
item.content:encoded: Rexel (RXL.PA) a relevé jeudi ses objectifs annuels pour la deuxième fois cette année, la forte demande des centres de données aux États-Unis et l'essor de l'électrification en Europe ayant porté les ventes trimestrielles du distributeur français de matériel électrique de 11,4% sur un an. "Ces résultats illustrent la manière dont notre repositionnement stratégique vers des segments à forte croissance et des services à valeur ajoutée a transformé le modèle économique de Rexel et accru sa visibilité", se félicite Guillaume Texier, directeur général, cité dans un communiqué du groupe. "Les acquisitions réalisées et annoncées en 2026, notamment GCG, vont encore accélérer notre transformation", ajoute le dirigeant. Pour les neuf premiers mois de l'année, les ventes du groupe grimpent de 7,3% sur un an à 15,44 milliards d'euros, les États-Unis affichant une croissance de 10,7% à 6,08 milliards et l'Europe de 3,2% à 7,15 milliards d'euros. Rexel vise désormais une croissance annuelle des ventes à environ 7%, ainsi qu'une marge d'Ebitda ajustée d'au moins 6,4%. En [USN:FWN43T17C TEXT:"juillet"], le groupe avait déjà relevé ses objectifs. "AUCUN SIGNE DE RALENTISSEMENT", SELON LE DG "Il y a un assez fort contraste entre la nervosité des marchés financiers et ce qu'on peut lire ici ou là sur le contexte économique et des résultat solides qui ne présentent vraiment aucun signe de faiblesse ou de ralentissement", a déclaré Guillaume Texier à Reuters. Le dirigeant a précisé que les États-Unis restaient au cœur du développement mondial des centres de données, car les plus grands investisseurs, notamment les hyperscalers, développaient principalement leurs capacités sur leur marché national. La croissance européenne de Rexel est portée par ce que Guillaume Texier a qualifié de transition structurelle vers l’électrification, la demande en pompes à chaleur, panneaux solaires, chargeurs de véhicules électriques et systèmes de climatisation ne cessant de croître. Le directeur général a par ailleurs indiqué que [USN:FWN45H0KO TEXT:"l’acquisition de GCG"] apporterait plus d’un milliard d’euros de chiffre d’affaires et qu’elle devrait être finalisée d’ici fin 2026. L’opération a été partiellement financée par une cession d’actions de 500 millions d’euros, ce qui laisse une marge de manœuvre pour de nouvelles acquisitions.

item.title: Norsk Hydro flags higher smelting costs after quarterly profit miss
item.description: Norwegian aluminium producer Norsk Hydro on Friday reported a third-quarter core profit below market expectations and said it expected higher costs and lower realised metal prices at its smelting business in the fourth quarter.
item.dc:creator: Jesus Calero
item.content:encoded: Norwegian aluminium producer Norsk Hydro (NHY.OL) on Friday reported a third-quarter core profit below market expectations and said it expected higher costs and lower realised metal prices at its smelting business in the fourth quarter. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose 51.6% from a year ago to 9.09 billion Norwegian crowns ($974.3 million), but missed analysts' average forecast of 9.53 billion crowns in a company-compiled poll . Disruption to Gulf aluminium supplies has lifted the premiums European buyers pay for metal, while expanding alumina production in China and Indonesia has weighed on prices for the raw material used to make it. Hydro is restarting smelting capacity in Slovakia and investing in Norwegian production of aluminium for Europe's electricity grids as the region seeks more secure supplies. Yet gas supply problems at its Brazilian refinery and a dispute over sales from its Qatar joint venture have exposed vulnerabilities in Hydro's own operations. COSTS RISING IN FOURTH QUARTER Hydro expects the premium it earns above benchmark aluminium prices to fall to between $550 and $600 a ton in the fourth quarter, from $673 in the previous three months. Its smelting division expects carbon costs to rise by 250-350 million crowns, alumina costs by 100-200 million crowns and fixed costs by 150-250 million crowns from the third quarter. It also expects higher sales volumes. The Alunorte alumina refinery in Brazil has returned to full production, but Hydro maintained its estimate of a $90 million to $110 million fourth-quarter hit from buying gas above contracted prices. That follows an around $85 million hit from gas supply disruptions and more expensive replacement purchases in the third quarter. Hydro slashed its 2026 capital spending forecast by 1 billion crowns to 12.5 billion, while raising year-end working capital guidance by 2 billion crowns to 32 billion. Free cash flow was 1.4 billion crowns in the quarter, constrained by higher metal prices that increased working capital requirements and prepayments. ($1 = 9.3302 Norwegian crowns)

item.title: Safran annonce des ventes en hausse de 13% au T3
item.description: Safran a fait état vendredi de ventes légèrement supérieures aux attentes au troisième trimestre, nourries par ses activités de construction et maintenance de moteurs.
item.dc:creator: Florence Loeve
item.content:encoded: Safran (SAF.PA) a fait état vendredi de ventes légèrement supérieures aux attentes au troisième trimestre, nourries par ses activités de construction et maintenance de moteurs. Le groupe aéronautique français, qui produit des moteurs pour avions et hélicoptères civils et militaires, des lanceurs de satellites et des propulseurs pour missiles, a indiqué que ses ventes se sont établies à 9 milliards d'euros sur la période juillet-septembre, en hausse organique de 13,4%. Des analystes anticipaient en moyenne des ventes de 8,99 milliards d'euros, selon un consensus publié par Safran sur son site internet. Safran a déclaré dans un communiqué que sa croissance était "portée par la montée en cadence de la production et la solide dynamique de l'après-vente pour moteurs civils". L'après-vente désigne les activités de maintenance, la fourniture de pièces de rechange ou les services techniques que Safran vend pour ses moteurs, et qui représentent une part importante de son activité. Au troisième trimestre, le chiffre d'affaires de la division "Propulsion" - qui représente plus de la moitié des ventes et comprend notamment ces activités - a augmenté de 13,2% en organique, dont une croissance de 18,7% pour l'après-vente. Via une co-entreprise baptisée CFM International, Safran développe avec l'Américain GE Aerospace les moteurs CFM56 et son successeur, le LEAP, utilisés par Airbus et Boeing pour leurs court et moyen-courriers. "Dans le secteur de la défense, nos activités bénéficient d'un marché porteur, et nous renforçons nos capacités de production pour préparer la croissance à venir", a déclaré le directeur général, Olivier Andriès, cité dans le communiqué.

item.title: BOJ chief Ueda to speak at IMF lecture on November 6
item.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda is scheduled to speak at the International Monetary Fund's central banking lecture in Washington on November 6, the central bank said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda is scheduled to speak at the International Monetary Fund's central banking lecture in Washington on November 6, the central bank said on Friday. After delivering a speech, Ueda will hold a conversation with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, according to the IMF's announcement posted on its website. The event will follow the BOJ's two-day policy meeting concluding on October 30. A subsequent meeting will be held on December 17-18. item.title: Sodexo-Le CA annuel dépasse les attentes, soutenu par les hausses de prix

item.title: Japan to simulate cyberattacks as PHP flaws roil global internet
item.description: Japan said on Friday it will set up a team to simulate cyberattacks using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems as organisations scramble to curtail risks from flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan said on Friday it will set up a team to simulate cyberattacks using AI to identify weaknesses in technology systems as organisations scramble to curtail risks from flaws in the [USN:L6N467127 TEXT:"PHP"] programming language that underpins much of the internet. [USN:L6N4670DM TEXT:"Government and company websites"] across the world went offline this week after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in the widely used programming language prompted millions of hacking attempts, forcing website operators to rush to protect or temporarily shut down their systems. Highlighting the extent of the disruption, Japanese mobile carrier SoftBank (9434.T) said on Friday it was suspending its emergency alert system for mobile users. That means customers will not receive early warnings for earthquakes, tsunami alerts or disaster and evacuation information as the system undergoes maintenance to address a PHP vulnerability, SoftBank said. "An attack can succeed by getting through just one hole ... for that reason it's important we shift our mindset and think from the perspective of the attacker," Japanese industry minister Ryosei Akazawa said on Friday. "Defenders also need to make use of AI and respond proactively, staying one step ahead." Emergency shutdowns this week from Tokyo to [USN:L6N467188 TEXT:"Helsinki"] of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services marked one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running. Companies including brokerage Nomura (8604.T) , lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (8306.T) , airline ANA (9202.T) and East Japan Railway (JR East) (9020.T) temporarily suspended some internet services as part of emergency measures. Japan's Ministry of Finance, National Tax Agency and Meteorological Agency also suspended some online services. On Friday, JR East said some group services had resumed while others would be restored once confirmed safe. Nippon Paint (4612.T) said it had applied a security patch as a precaution and its website is back online. Attackers are likely targeting Japanese businesses for their thorough records, which are no longer protected by a language barrier because of AI, said Eva Chen, CEO of Trend Micro (4704.T) . Japan has been too comfortable with its existing infrastructure, which it felt was safe enough, she said. Cybersecurity experts have said [USN:L1N45U0IU TEXT:"AI is helping attackers"] automate tasks from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect. The developers of PHP - a computing language like HTML and Python - released [USN:L6N4670ZW TEXT:"fixes"] on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI. They urged users to "update immediately".

item.title: Electrolux reports Q3 core profit beat, says North America weakness persists
item.description: Swedish home appliance maker Electrolux beat expectations for third-quarter core profit on Friday helped by cost savings, but flagged that demand in its key North America region continued to weaken.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swedish home appliance maker Electrolux (ELUXb.ST) beat expectations for third-quarter core profit on Friday helped by cost savings, but flagged that demand in its key North America region continued to weaken. "Competitive pressure remained high, alongside significant cost headwinds from external factors, including raw material, logistic costs and U.S. tariffs," President and CEO Yannick Fierling said in a statement. Quarterly adjusted operating income came in at 912 million Swedish crowns ($92 million), against 867 million expected by analysts in a company-compiled poll, with organic sales growing 3.5%. Electrolux, under pressure from cautious consumer behaviour, cut-price competition and rising costs, has been restructuring its business and cutting costs. The company said that inflation worries continued to dent consumer confidence in North America, a region that accounted for 35% of group sales in the quarter. Fierling said customers in the region had shifted toward "lower price points", prioritizing affordability. Sales in the region were up 2%, but mainly driven by price increases, Electrolux said. Consumer confidence in the United States has fallen to the lowest level since 2014, a survey [USN:L1N45L0LX TEXT:"showed"] in September, amid pressure from high interest rates, increased energy prices and costs of living. Home appliance makers in the country also [USN:L4N41K1J4 TEXT:"faced"] product discounting earlier in the year, which squeezed their margins. Electrolux now expects prices and volumes to have a neutral impact on its result in 2026, having previously expected a positive contribution. ($1 = 9.9195 Swedish crowns)

item.title: Volvo Cars to cut 2,500 jobs as third quarter swings to loss
item.description: Volvo Cars said on Friday it will cut 2,500 jobs, mostly in its native Sweden, as the group seeks to slash costs amid tough competition from Chinese auto makers and as tariffs and weak demand hit sales in the United States.
item.dc:creator: Marie Mannes
item.content:encoded: Volvo Cars (VOLCARb.ST) said on Friday it will cut 2,500 jobs, mostly in its native Sweden, as the group seeks to slash costs amid tough competition from Chinese auto makers and as tariffs and weak demand hit sales in the United States. The company, majority-owned by China's Geely Holding (GEELY.UL), reported an adjusted operating loss of 3.7 billion Swedish crowns ($373 million) for the third quarter, down from a profit of 5.8 billion crowns a year earlier. Volvo said that in addition to its earlier cost reductions it will cut an additional 5 billion crowns in indirect spend and variable costs, which it expects to be realised by the end of next year. Some 2,500 jobs will be lost globally, of which 2,000 are in Sweden as the group ends consultant contracts, applies natural attrition and offers "targeted exit packages" to employees, Volvo Cars said in a statement. The group has long struggled to stay profitable amid cooling demand for electric vehicles (EV), tough conditions in China - where revenue fell by almost 50% in the third quarter - and the strain of high costs and tariffs. "The third quarter of 2026 was very disappointing and reflects a year that has become far more challenging than originally anticipated. Our ongoing turnaround plan therefore needs a decisive reinforcement," CEO Hakan Samuelsson said. Volvo Cars earlier this month [USN:L6N45O0BV TEXT:"scrapped its guidance"] for full-year sales volume and cash flow owing to what it said was an increasingly challenging market and deteriorating near-term outlook. The new layoffs come on top of the [USN:L5N3RY0I2 TEXT:"3,000 job cuts"] announced shortly after Samuelsson returned as CEO in 2025, when Volvo [USN:L8N3R60KQ TEXT:"tightened costs"] across the company with an 18 billion crown savings plan and deepened cooperation with Geely brands. Volvo's gross margin, a metric closely watched by investors to gauge the impact of tariffs and discounting, came in at 14.7% in the third quarter, compared to 20.4% last year. The group's share price hit a record low this week and is down 54% year-to-date, burdened by tariffs , weaker EV demand and high development costs. ($1 = 9.9195 Swedish crowns)

item.title: Safran posts slightly higher than expected Q3 sales
item.description: French jet engine maker Safran posted slightly higher-than-expected third-quarter revenue on Friday, driven by its core jet engine division, and confirmed its 2026 outlook.
item.dc:creator: Florence Loeve, Joanna Plucinska
item.content:encoded: French jet engine maker Safran (SAF.PA) posted slightly higher-than-expected third-quarter revenue on Friday, driven by its core jet engine division, and confirmed its 2026 outlook. One of the world's largest aerospace equipment suppliers, Safran said sales for the third quarter of the year grew organically by 13.4% to €9 billion ($10.09 billion). Analysts were on average expecting quarterly sales of €8.99 billion, according to a company-compiled consensus. Safran raised its targets in July, projecting revenue growth in the mid-teens percentage range with recurring operating income between €6.4 billion and €6.5 billion, after it posted stronger-than-expected first-half profits driven by demand for spare parts. The results show that demand for spare parts and maintenance on older engines is still driving profits at Safran and other engine makers. Safran's propulsion division, which accounted for half of its revenue in 2025, reported 13.2% organic sales growth for the third quarter, with aftermarket revenue rising by 18.7%. "Civil engine spare parts continue to perform well, driven by sustained investment in maintenance from airlines, supporting our view of a strong and durable aftermarket environment," Chief Executive Olivier Andries said in a statement. CFM, a joint venture between Safran and GE Aerospace (GE.N) and the world's largest jet engine maker by units sold, is reaping maintenance profits from its CFM56 jet engines, which continue to power thousands of planes even though CFM's newer LEAP engine has replaced them on current Boeing and Airbus narrow-body jet deliveries. GE Aerospace on Tuesday [USN:L4N4660OA TEXT:"raised"] its 2026 profit forecast for the second time this year, as demand for aircraft engine repairs and spare parts remained strong despite surging fuel costs that have squeezed airline profits. Safran's Equipment and Defence division generated €3.6 billion in quarterly revenue, slightly above the €3.5 billion expected by analysts. "In defense, our activities are benefiting from robust market dynamics, and we are expanding our production capabilities to prepare for future growth," Andries added. ($1 = 0.8921 euros)

item.content:encoded: Sodexo (EXHO.PA) reported stronger-than-expected full-year revenue on Friday, helped by steady demand and higher prices, as Chief Executive Thierry Delaporte pressed ahead with efforts to rebuild competitiveness after contract losses and weaker performance in the group's key North American market. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's record 20-point streak ends as Thunder beat Nuggets
item.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored just 17 points to snap an NBA-record streak, but the Oklahoma City Thunder knocked off the Denver Nuggets 96-84 at home Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored just 17 points to snap an NBA-record streak, but the Oklahoma City Thunder knocked off the Denver Nuggets 96-84 at home Thursday. Gilgeous-Alexander had scored 20 or more points in an NBA-record 141 consecutive games. He hadn't been held below 20 points in the regular season since Oct. 30, 2024. Gilgeous-Alexander had a chance to extend the streak, but with less than two minutes remaining and Oklahoma City up by 17, Nuggets coach David Adelman emptied his bench following a timeout. The reigning two-time NBA Most Valuable Player didn't wait for direction from Thunder coach Mark Daigneault, taking his place on the bench to officially end the streak. To that point, Gilgeous-Alexander had been making a strong push toward keeping the streak alive with 10 fourth-quarter points. Oklahoma City hadn't led since going up 3-0 in the opening seconds until Ajay Mitchell's transition layup with just more than two minutes remaining in the third quarter. In the closing seconds of the third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander raced up the court after a rebound from Jaylin Williams and drained a 3-pointer in transition to put the Thunder up by six. Gilgeous-Alexander had been 0-for-7 from beyond the arc before hitting the shot. Gilgeous-Alexander was initially called for a foul on Nikola Jokic's 3-point heave as time expired in the quarter, which would have given Jokic three free throws, but the play was challenged and the foul call was overturned. Gilgeous-Alexander missed all seven shots he attempted in the first half and didn't get on the board at all until sinking a pair of free throws with less than two minutes remaining. Gilgeous-Alexander quickly broke that stretch without a field goal in the third quarter, but it wasn't until that 3-pointer late in the period that he found an offensive rhythm. It didn't matter, though, as the Thunder forced 13 second-half turnovers and turned them into 19 points. Oklahoma City scored 14 of its 26 fourth-quarter points off takeaways. Jalen Williams led Oklahoma City with 21 points while Chet Holmgren had 12 points and 17 rebounds. The Thunder hit just 11 of 43 (25.6%) from behind the 3-point arc. Aaron Gordon led the Nuggets with 20 points while Jokic had 13 points on 5-of-19 shooting. Denver's Cameron Johnson left with 3:30 remaining in the second quarter after sustaining a right ankle sprain. He did not return. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rolls-Royce nears government subsidy deal to develop new engine in UK, FT reports
item.description: Rolls-Royce is nearing a deal for British government subsidies of up to £200 million ($267.9 million) to help fund the development of a new engine for short-haul aircraft, with an announcement possible as early as next week, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

item.title: Holcim raises earnings forecast after Q3 profit beats expectations
item.description: Swiss cement maker Holcim raised its full-year earnings forecast on Friday after reporting better-than-expected quarterly sales and profit as it sold more higher-margin low-carbon products.
item.dc:creator: John Revill
item.content:encoded: Swiss cement maker Holcim (HOLN.S) raised its full-year earnings forecast on Friday after reporting better-than-expected quarterly sales and profit as it sold more higher-margin low-carbon products. Shares were set to open 4.8% higher premarket in Zurich. The results of Holcim, one of the world's biggest construction materials companies, give an insight into the health of the broader building industry. The company posted a 27% increase in its sales of building solutions products - roofs, walling and flooring - which are highly profitable when sold as a package of products to builders and are less capital-intensive to produce. As a result, Holcim increased its profit margin in the three months to September 30, pushing recurring operating profit 17% higher to 976 million Swiss francs ($1.19 billion). That beat analyst expectations of 949 million francs in a company-compiled consensus. Sales rose to 4.66 billion francs, Holcim said, above estimates of 4.59 billion francs. As a result, Holcim increased its full-year earnings forecast, saying it now expects its recurring operating profit to increase 10%-12%, up from its previous expectation of a 10% increase. This is the second time this year that Holcim has increased its profit forecast, following an upgrade in [USN:L8N43X09P TEXT:"July"]. The company has improved its performance by selling more low-carbon cement and concrete, which boast higher profit margins, while increasing its usage of recycled building materials. "In the first nine months of the year, we achieved strong profitable growth with an industry-leading recurring EBIT margin thanks to increased customer demand for our high-value offering, strict cost discipline and operational excellence," said CEO Miljan Gutovic. Holcim reported higher quarterly sales and profit in all three of its regions, with the company saying it was seeing a strong pipeline of infrastructure projects in Europe and Latin America, while it expects further growth from investments in Morocco related to the 2030 football World Cup. "The raised EBIT growth guidance was expected and consensus already sits there, but fears of a potential downward revision had flared up recently and proved unfounded, so today's solid Q3 and guidance hike should be taken positively," said Bank Vontobel analyst Mark Diethelm. ($1 = 0.8209 Swiss francs)

item.title: Morning Bid: Wake up! The long bond's up two points!
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole. It's not every day you wake up to see the US long bond up 2 full points in price, but that's what happened overnight. Ten-year yields dived 19 basis points in the biggest daily move since early 2023, when Silicon Valley Bank collapsed. Fed funds futures rallied as much as 22 ticks, essentially taking an entire hike off the table for next year, while a December move is no longer fully priced in. Old-fashioned safe harbours were in demand as the yen and Swiss franc climbed, leaving the dollar looking a little less exceptional. The proximate cause this time was the sound of air escaping from the [USN:L6N4681D7 TEXT:"AI bubble"] as investors grappled with the sheer scale of funding needed for all this compute power. Some estimates put it at 1.6 times the cost of laying America's railways. Seems [USN:L6N468125 TEXT:"Meta's"] mention of needing "hundreds of billions of dollars" for capex [USN:L4N4681N3 TEXT:"spooked the horses"], with its shares sliding almost 7%. And not everyone was happy about the dilution from having to establish a whole new class of stock with no voting rights to raise the money. CoreWeave, the data center group that started much of this scare, shed another 10% of its value to hit lows last seen in May 2025, while credit spreads blew out across the entire sector. Treasuries benefited from the resulting scramble for safety, though that "safety" is relative these days. There is also the risk the investment boom in data centres will sputter, stalling a major driver of economic growth. Voter opposition to the energy-hungry sites has also been a notable feature of the midterm campaigns, adding politics to the mix. The surge in Treasuries might bring back memories of the Greenspan put, but it'll be much harder for the Fed to ride to the rescue this time. Brent futures are atop $113 a barrel, and over $100 right out to March, while crude for actual delivery is far higher. Easing monetary policy during an inflationary oil shock is going to be a hard sell. Neither is there any end in sight to the conflict in the Gulf. The press is full of reports of the White House considering fresh attacks on Iran after the midterms. The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group just departed Japan this week for Exercise Keen Sword 27, after which it will head for the Middle East. Ever since the war started in February, analysts have always assumed it would be done within a month or maybe two. Next week will mark the eighth month of the war, and it's not even clear whether Washington and Tehran are talking to each other. That will ensure inflation is front and centre when the Fed meets next week, relegating Wall Street's woes to a footnote. Key developments that could influence markets on Friday: - October global PMIs for Europe, UK and US. UK and Canada retail sales - Appearance by ECB board member Piero Cipollone (This story has been corrected to fix a typo in paragraph 5.)

item.title: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins leads Oilers over Hurricanes with shootout goal
item.description: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins converted for a shootout goal to complete a special return to the lineup as the Edmonton Oilers defeated the visiting Carolina Hurricanes 6-5 on Thursday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins converted for a shootout goal to complete a special return to the lineup as the Edmonton Oilers defeated the visiting Carolina Hurricanes 6-5 on Thursday night. Leon Draisaitl and Connor McDavid each provided two goals and three assists, and Nugent-Hopkins also notched a goal and an assist in regulation in his season debut for the Oilers. Both of Draisaitl's goals came on power plays. McDavid added to his record-setting assist total -- now at 23 -- across the first 10 games of the season. Carolina's Seth Jarvis scored in his first outing of the season, Sebastian Aho had a goal and an assist, and Jackson Blake, Logan Stankoven and Juuso Valimaki also scored for the Hurricanes. Jordan Martinook and Shayne Gostisbehere each assisted on two goals. Oilers goalie Devon Levi stopped 22 shots. Brandon Bussi made 16 saves for Carolina. With McDavid and Draisaitl converting, the Oilers scored twice in the first three minutes of the third period to pull even at 4-4. Valimaki, in his second game for the Hurricanes, put Carolina up 5-4 with 2:40 remaining in the third period. McDavid tied it with 1:28 left. Jarvis, a winger who was Carolina's leading goal-scorer last season and was activated for the first time since offseason shoulder surgery, broke a 2-2 tie with 7:01 remaining in the second period. He made a spin move from the right side around Edmonton defenseman Evan Bouchard and then beat Levi for the goal. The offense began early. With Carolina's Nicolas Deslauriers in the penalty box for tripping, the Oilers converted on the game's first power play with Draisaitl scoring 8:07 into the game. Less than 2 1/2 minutes later, the Hurricanes countered with Blake's power-play goal. At that juncture, Blake had half of Carolina's six shots on goal. The Oilers finished the first period with four shots. After Aho put the Hurricanes ahead with an unassisted goal 30 seconds into the second period, Nugent-Hopkins countered with a power-play goal at 4:20 of the second period. Jarvis and Stankoven scored later in the period for Carolina's 4-2 lead. The Hurricanes had Skyler Brind'Amour, son of coach Rod Brind'Amour, in the lineup for the first time this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: India's Zetwerk slips below IPO price in debut, valued at $2.7 billion
